description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish red lentil soup, known for its vibrant color and comforting taste. This wholesome dish is incredibly easy to prepare, offering a rich, earthy flavor with a hint of mint and a touch of spice. It is a staple in Turkish homes, perfect as a starter or a light, satisfying meal.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear; drain well. Chop the onion finely and mince the garlic cloves. Have your tomato paste and flour ready.

instructions.title: Sauté Vegetables
instructions.text: In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil or butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Add Flour and Tomato Paste
instructions.text: Stir in the all-purpose flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to cook out the raw flour taste. Add the tomato paste and cook for another minute, stirring to combine with the onion mixture.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup Base
instructions.text: Add the rinsed lentils to the pot, then pour in the 6 cups of water or vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Use an immersion blender to blend the soup directly in the pot until it is smooth and creamy. Alternatively, carefully transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. Season with salt, black pepper, and 1 teaspoon of dried mint and 1/2 teaspoon of red pepper flakes.

instructions.title: Prepare the Spiced Butter Topping
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, add 1 teaspoon of dried mint and 1 teaspoon of red pepper flakes (pul biber). Sauté for about 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle each serving with a spoonful of the spiced butter topping. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing, which adds a wonderful brightness to the soup.

tips: For an extra creamy texture, ensure your lentils are cooked until very soft before blending. If using a regular blender, be cautious with hot liquids and blend in small batches.
The spiced butter topping (nane yagli sos) is essential for an authentic Turkish flavor. Do not skip it, as it adds a beautiful aroma and a touch of richness.
Always serve Mercimek Corbasi with fresh lemon wedges. A squeeze of lemon juice brightens the flavors and balances the richness of the soup beautifully.
article:
# Mercimek Corbasi: The Soul-Warming Delight of Turkish Red Lentil Soup

In the vast and varied tapestry of Turkish cuisine, few dishes hold a place as cherished and comforting as Mercimek Corbasi, the beloved Turkish Red Lentil Soup. This vibrant, aromatic, and incredibly nourishing soup is a staple in every Turkish household, a consistent presence on restaurant menus, and a warm hug in a bowl that transcends seasons and occasions. Whether enjoyed as a hearty breakfast, a satisfying lunch, or a comforting start to dinner, Mercimek Corbasi embodies the essence of Turkish hospitality and culinary simplicity.

This article will guide you through the rich history, essential ingredients, and step-by-step preparation of this iconic soup, ensuring you can recreate its authentic magic in your own kitchen. Prepare to embark on a culinary journey that promises warmth, flavor, and a taste of Turkey's heartwarming traditions.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi (Turkish Red Lentil Soup)?

Mercimek Corbasi, pronounced "mer-jee-mek chor-ba-see," translates directly to "lentil soup." While various lentil soups exist in Turkey, the red lentil version is by far the most popular and recognized. It's a creamy, savory, and subtly spiced pureed soup made primarily from red lentils, onions, garlic, and a touch of tomato paste, often finished with a distinctive melted butter and dried mint (nane) topping.

Its allure lies in its humble ingredients and profound flavor. Red lentils, known for their quick cooking time and ability to break down into a creamy consistency, form the backbone of the soup. The meticulous sautéing of onions and garlic provides a sweet and pungent base, while a spoonful of rich tomato paste (salça) adds umami depth and a beautiful reddish hue. The final flourish of butter infused with dried mint and sometimes paprika or Aleppo pepper (pul biber) is not merely a garnish; it’s an integral part of the experience, contributing a fragrant, herbaceous counterpoint that elevates the entire dish.

More than just a soup, Mercimek Corbasi is a symbol of home, comfort, and nourishment. It's often the first solid food given to babies in Turkey and a go-to remedy for colds or simply a chilly day. Its widespread appeal speaks to its perfect balance of flavor, ease of preparation, and health benefits, making it an indispensable part of Turkish culinary heritage.

## Ingredients for Authentic Turkish Red Lentil Soup

The beauty of Mercimek Corbasi lies in its simplicity. You don't need exotic ingredients to create this authentic taste; just a few pantry staples transform into something truly extraordinary.

Here’s what you’ll need:

*   **Red Lentils:** About 1 cup. These are crucial. They cook quickly and break down easily, giving the soup its characteristic creamy texture. Ensure they are well-rinsed.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped. Forms the aromatic base.
*   **Garlic:** 2-3 cloves, minced. Adds depth and pungency.
*   **Tomato Paste (Salça):** 1 tablespoon. A key ingredient for color and umami. Turkish tomato paste is often richer and less sweet than some Western varieties.
*   **Olive Oil:** 2 tablespoons, for sautéing.
*   **Butter:** 2 tablespoons, for the finishing oil (nane yağı).
*   **Dried Mint (Nane):** 1-2 teaspoons, for the finishing oil. Don't skip this; it's essential for authentic flavor.
*   **Paprika (Tatlı Pul Biber or Kırmızı Toz Biber):** 1 teaspoon, optional, for the finishing oil. Adds a gentle warmth and color. Hot chili flakes (acı pul biber) can be used for heat.
*   **Water or Vegetable Broth:** 6-7 cups. Broth will add more flavor, but water is traditionally used and works perfectly well.
*   **Salt:** To taste.
*   **Black Pepper:** To taste.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** For serving, a squeeze of fresh lemon is non-negotiable!

## How to Make Mercimek Corbasi: Step-by-Step Instructions

Making this Turkish Red Lentil Soup is a straightforward process that yields incredibly rewarding results.

**Step 1: Prepare the Lentils**
Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes excess starch and prevents the soup from becoming cloudy. Drain well.

**Step 2: Sauté the Aromatics**
In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent, being careful not to brown them. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.

**Step 3: Build the Flavor Base**
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly. This step helps to deepen its flavor and mellow its raw taste. If using, add a pinch of paprika or chili flakes to the pot now to bloom their flavors.

**Step 4: Add Lentils and Liquid**
Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot, stirring to coat them with the onion, garlic, and tomato paste mixture. Pour in the water or vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

**Step 5: Blend the Soup**
Once the lentils are tender, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it reaches a smooth and creamy consistency. Alternatively, transfer the soup in batches to a standard blender (be cautious with hot liquids) and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot.

**Step 6: Season and Adjust**
Return the blended soup to low heat. Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Let it simmer gently for another 5 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.

**Step 7: Prepare the Nane Yağı (Mint Oil Topping)**
While the soup simmers, prepare the fragrant topping. In a small pan, melt the butter over medium-low heat. Once melted, add the dried mint and the remaining paprika (if using). Sauté for about 30 seconds to 1 minute, stirring constantly, until the mint is fragrant and slightly crispy. Be careful not to burn it.

**Step 8: Serve**
Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the aromatic nane yağı over each serving. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges and crusty bread.

## Tips for the Best Turkish Red Lentil Soup

Achieving that authentic, soul-satisfying flavor of Turkish Red Lentil Soup is easy with a few key tips:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils Thoroughly:** This is crucial. Unrinsed lentils can make your soup cloudy and sometimes impart an earthy flavor that some find unpleasant.
*   **Don't Skimp on the Tomato Paste:** Use good quality tomato paste, ideally Turkish salça, for the best depth of flavor and color. Cooking it for a minute or two before adding liquid helps to develop its richness.
*   **Bloom Your Spices:** Sautéing the dried mint and paprika in butter for the topping brings out their full aroma and flavor, transforming them from simple spices into a fragrant, delicious infusion.
*   **Blend Until Smooth:** While some prefer a chunkier lentil soup, authentic Mercimek Corbasi is typically velvety smooth. An immersion blender makes this step incredibly easy.
*   **A Squeeze of Lemon is Essential:** The acidity from fresh lemon juice brightens the flavors of the Turkish Red Lentil Soup, cutting through the richness and adding a vital tangy note that truly completes the dish. Never serve it without lemon wedges.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** As with all cooking, taste your soup before serving and adjust salt, pepper, or even a tiny pinch more dried mint if needed.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways throughout the day.

Traditionally, it's served hot, garnished with the vibrant nane yağı, and accompanied by:

*   **Fresh Lemon Wedges:** A generous squeeze of lemon is non-negotiable.
*   **Crusty Bread (Ekmek or Pide):** Perfect for dipping and soaking up every last drop.
*   **Pul Biber (Aleppo Pepper Flakes):** For those who like an extra kick of mild heat.
*   **Pickled Vegetables (Turşu):** The tanginess provides a wonderful contrast.
*   **Olives:** A simple side that complements the soup beautifully.

It makes a fantastic light lunch on its own, a warming starter for a larger Turkish meal, or even a comforting breakfast in Turkish homes. Pair it with a simple green salad (çoban salatası) for a complete and healthy meal.

## Variations and Dietary Adaptations

One of the many reasons Mercimek Corbasi is so beloved is its inherent flexibility and suitability for various dietary needs.

*   **Vegan/Vegetarian:** The traditional recipe is naturally vegan! Just ensure you use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth (if opting for broth over water).
*   **Gluten-Free:** Red lentils are naturally gluten-free, as are all the other core ingredients, making this soup an excellent choice for those avoiding gluten.
*   **Spicier Version:** To add more heat, increase the amount of hot pul biber (Aleppo pepper) or add a pinch of cayenne pepper with the tomato paste.
*   **Heartier Soup:** While traditionally smooth, you can add finely diced carrots or potatoes along with the lentils for extra substance and nutrition. Just ensure they cook through before blending.
*   **Herb Variations:** While dried mint is classic, a sprinkle of fresh parsley or dill can be added at the end for a different aromatic touch, though it will slightly alter the authentic profile.
*   **Different Lentils:** While red lentils are preferred for their creamy texture and quick cooking, brown or green lentils can be used, but they will require a longer cooking time and may result in a less smooth, more textured soup.

No matter how you choose to adapt it, the essence of the Turkish Red Lentil Soup remains: a wholesome, flavorful, and deeply satisfying dish that offers comfort in every spoonful.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a soup; it’s a culinary embrace, a testament to the power of simple ingredients transformed into something truly spectacular. Its warmth, nourishing qualities, and authentic Turkish flavors make it a dish worth mastering. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to be enchanted by the comforting magic of this timeless Turkish Red Lentil Soup. Afiyet olsun! (Bon appétit!)
